A0124.title: Real-Time On-Chain Rug Pull Detection
A0124.definition: Continuously collecting on-chain transactions, liquidity movements, and contract permission changes to identify Rug Pull indicators in real time through anomaly rules and risk models.
A0124.description: On-chain monitoring systems continuously collect liquidity-pool balances and lock periods, token-holder distribution, contract ownership and upgrade-permission changes, developer-address transfers, calls related to abnormal supply changes, and sell restrictions. The detection engine evaluates liquidity-drop thresholds, concentration rules, privileged-function call patterns, fund flows, and address-history baselines, while correlating project age, audit status, and team-address labels to reduce single-signal errors. When combinations such as abnormal supply movement, sharp liquidity-pool decline, or permission-configuration changes are detected, the system issues tiered alerts to exchanges, governance teams, and investors, records triggering rules, transaction hashes, and address evidence, and may initiate trading pauses, exposure limits, or manual review. Confirmed incidents are replayed to tune thresholds and models as attackers gradually move liquidity or transfer assets across multiple addresses.
A0124.limitation: On-chain detection is affected by block-confirmation and indexing delays. Attackers may evade rules by gradually moving liquidity, using cross-chain transfers, splitting addresses, or creating transaction patterns that imitate normal activity. New projects also lack stable behavioral baselines and may generate false positives, while an alert cannot guarantee that transfers will be blocked before funds leave.
